summary.title: Butterick's Practical Typography
summary.one_liner: A web-based book covering practical typography rules for documents and the web, from straight quotes and spacing to font choice and page layout.
takeaways: Learn concrete typographic rules for typing text, such as quotes, dashes, spacing and punctuation.
Find font recommendations and alternatives to common system fonts like Times New Roman, Helvetica and Georgia.
Understand page layout basics including line length, line spacing, margins, and widow and orphan control.
Consult the appendix and commentary for topics like making PDFs, embedding fonts, and screen-reading considerations.
summary.summary: This is an online book by Matthew Butterick that lays out practical typography guidance in a structured reference format. It is organized into sections on why typography matters, type composition (punctuation, spaces, dashes, special characters), text formatting (bold, italics, caps, headings, kerning), font recommendations with alternatives to common fonts, and page layout (margins, line spacing, lists, tables, styles). It also includes sample documents, an appendix on practical tasks such as making PDFs and embedding fonts, and commentary essays. The page text is a table of contents and does not show the full body text, and the site asks readers to pay for the book.
